newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front says no change in leadership.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front says no change in leadership.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition said on Friday that there had been no change in leadership as parliament neared a confidence vote in the government.

"There has been no change in leadership," Sitaram Yechury, a member of the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee, told reporters after coalition leaders met to discuss the political crisis.
Earlier on Friday, the 15-party United Front and Congress launched talks to try to find a successor to Deve Gowda, who faced near certain defeat in the vote of confidence due later in the day.

Leaders of both sides had earlier said a consensus candidate for the prime ministership could be named by the United Front before the vote or soon afterwards. United Front officials said Deve Gowda would face the vote.

"A vote will take place," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters. He said the coalition's Steering Committee would meet in the evening under Deve Gowda's chairmanship to take stock. Asked if the front was willing to "have truck" with Congress, Reddy said: "That depends on the meeting in the evening."
The chief minister of Andhra Pradesh state, Chandrababu Naidu, said he was not a candidate to succeed Deve Gowda. "I am not a candidate for the job," he said.
